intro.eyebrow: China's landscape in ink and water
intro.title: Guilin, Mountains Meet the River
intro.left: In southern China, the Li River winds between limestone peaks that rise almost vertically from the plain. The landscape has inspired Chinese painters and poets for centuries, creating the feeling of moving through a living ink-wash painting rather than a conventional scenic region.
intro.right: Guilin is best experienced outdoors: a river journey toward Yangshuo, cycling beside fields, bamboo rafting on the Yulong River, and walking through rice terraces or limestone caves. It suits travelers who want to slow down, leave the megacities behind, and let the landscape set the pace.

stay.title: How long to stay
stay.summary: Three or four days connect Guilin and Yangshuo; a fifth leaves room for the Longji terraces.

plans.label: 3 days
plans.summary: See Guilin’s city landmarks, travel the Li River, and spend unhurried time in Yangshuo.

plans.label: 4 days
plans.summary: Add Yulong River, countryside cycling, a cave, and a slower evening in Yangshuo.

plans.label: 5 days
plans.summary: Add the Longji Rice Terraces with an overnight or well-timed private transfer.

items.label: Getting there
items.summary: Guilin has an airport and high-speed rail stations; Yangshuo is reached by rail or road transfer.

items.label: Getting around
items.summary: Use Guilin for arrival and Yangshuo for countryside days. Transfers take longer than map distances suggest.

items.label: Where to stay
items.summary: Stay near the Li River in Guilin, then move to Yangshuo rather than commuting every day.

items.label: Planning ahead
items.summary: Rain creates atmospheric scenery but can affect river and mountain activities, so keep one flexible day.
